children: U.S. stocks rose despite tech sector volatility and a hot wholesale inflation reading as Treasury yields gave back some recent gains.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 556.80 points, or 1.08%, to 52178.28, and the S&P 500 gained 25.17 points, or 0.33%, to 7744.11, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite edged 20.16 points, or 0.08%, 26713.03.

The producer-price index rose by 1.3% in September on a month-to-month basis, far above both the 0.4% increase in August and economists' expectations of 0.6%. It was the largest increase in the gauge in more than four years.
Investors piled into safe havens on Thursday following the tech wobbles and inflation scares.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond dropped 0.102 percentage point to 5.086%, the largest one-day retreat in more than a year, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The yield on the 30-year bond slipped 0.097 percentage point to 5.427%, also the biggest drop in more than a year. The two-year Treasury's yield declined 0.053 percentage point to 4.747%, which was the biggest decline in two weeks.
Gold futures, another safe haven that had been under pressure in recent weeks, rose $62.90, or 1.5% to $4147.70 a troy ounce.
